opening.text: Imagine two people setting out on a long hike. The trail is steep in places. There are muddy stretches and a few wrong turns. Some days the weather is perfect. Other days it rains. But the two keep walking, side by side, and they carry each other’s load when one is tired.
That is a good picture of marriage. It is not a short walk. It is a long trail, and it is walked together.

mainMessage.text: Marriage is a journey that lasts. It grows as we grow in love for the Savior, in patience and in the help of the Holy Ghost. We do not need to be perfect. We need to keep walking together.

blocks.text: **Two people, side by side.** On a trail, one hiker does not walk far ahead of the other. They stay close. In marriage, husband and wife walk together as equals. Neither is above or below the other.
And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.
Elder Ulisses Soares, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “In Partnership with the Lord” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
They walk side by side, as equals, the divine offspring of God.
We walk side by side.
**The trail is long.** Nobody finishes a mountain trail in the first hour. Marriage is the same. It does not end at the wedding. The wedding is where the walking starts.
Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.
Elder Neil L. Andersen, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Eternal marriage is an eternal journey.
The journey is long, and that is all right.
**A better map.** Hikers who love the mountain tend to love the people they hike with. In the same way, the more we love the Savior, the more we love each other. He shows us how to love.
But charity is the pure love of Christ, and it endureth forever; and whoso is found possessed of it at the last day, it shall be well with him.
Elder Neil L. Andersen, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
As we increase our love for the Savior, our love for each other grows.
Love for Him makes love for each other grow.
**Slow stretches.** Some parts of the trail are slow and hard. A good hiker does not quit. He slows down and keeps going. Patience is one of the gifts of the Spirit, and marriage needs it.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,
Elder Neil L. Andersen, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
There are times in our marriage that require a stellar dose of patience.
Patience gets us through the slow stretches.
**A guide on the trail.** A good guide knows the path. The Holy Ghost knows what a husband and wife need. When we invite Him into our marriage, He shows us the next step.
For behold, again I say unto you that if ye will enter in by the way, and receive the Holy Ghost, it will show unto you all things what ye should do.
Elder Neil L. Andersen, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
We profoundly need the gift of the Holy Ghost in our personal lives and in our marriage.
He is the guide we need.
**The summit is worth it.** Hikers keep going because they know what waits at the top. Hope keeps a couple moving. It is hope in each other and in the Savior.
Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.
Elder Neil L. Andersen, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Keep your hope in each other and in Jesus Christ.
Hope keeps us walking.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when a marriage, their own or another, held steady through a hard stretch. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Isaac and Rebekah

blocks.text: Isaac was grieving his mother when Rebekah came into his life. The scripture is short, but it says much.
And Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah’s tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife; and he loved her: and Isaac was comforted after his mother’s death.
Rebekah’s love comforted Isaac. A good marriage gives comfort on hard days.

application.text: First, do one kind thing for your spouse this week without being asked. If you are not married, do one kind thing for someone close to you.
Second, pray together, or pray for each other by name, every day this week.
Third, if a stretch of the trail feels too hard, do not walk it alone. Speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that marriage is a gift from God. I know that He helps husbands and wives who turn to Him. I have seen that love for the Savior makes love at home stronger. I know that Jesus Christ walks with us. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A two-person canoe only works when both people paddle. If one stops, the canoe drifts. If they paddle on opposite sides without talking, it zigzags. But when both lean in and keep the same rhythm, the canoe glides.
Marriage is a lot like that. Two people, one boat, and a long river.

mainMessage.text: A strong marriage is built by two people paddling together. Love for the Savior sets the rhythm. Patience and the Holy Ghost help us through the rapids. Hope carries us to the end.

blocks.text: **Both paddle.** In a canoe, neither person sits back and lets the other do all the work. In marriage, husband and wife are equals. They share the load and the direction.
And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.
Elder Ulisses Soares, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “In Partnership with the Lord” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
They walk side by side, as equals, the divine offspring of God.
Two paddles, one boat.
**The river does not end.** A river runs on past every bend. Marriage keeps going too. It has new bends, new stretches and new views. It is a lifelong trip, and beyond.
Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.
Elder Neil L. Andersen, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Eternal marriage is an eternal journey.
There is always another bend.
**Keep the rhythm.** A canoe needs a steady rhythm. For a couple, that rhythm is love for the Savior. When it is strong, the two stay in step.
But charity is the pure love of Christ, and it endureth forever; and whoso is found possessed of it at the last day, it shall be well with him.
Elder Neil L. Andersen, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
As we increase our love for the Savior, our love for each other grows.
His love sets the rhythm.
**Calm water takes patience.** Not every stretch of river is exciting. Some are slow. A couple needs patience for the long, flat parts, and for the rapids too.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,
Elder Neil L. Andersen, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
There are times in our marriage that require a stellar dose of patience.
Patience keeps the canoe steady.
**Read the water.** Rapids look different from above. A guide on the bank sees what the paddlers cannot. The Holy Ghost sees what we miss. He can warn us and guide us.
For behold, again I say unto you that if ye will enter in by the way, and receive the Holy Ghost, it will show unto you all things what ye should do.
Elder Neil L. Andersen, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
We profoundly need the gift of the Holy Ghost in our personal lives and in our marriage.
He helps us read the water.
**Keep your eyes ahead.** A paddler who looks only at the rocks hits the rocks. A couple that keeps its eyes on hope, in each other and in Christ, stays on course.
Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.
Elder Neil L. Andersen, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Keep your hope in each other and in Jesus Christ.
Hope keeps us on course.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when a husband and wife learned to work as a team. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Aquila and Priscilla

blocks.text: Aquila and Priscilla were a married couple who served the Lord together. They heard a gifted speaker named Apollos and wanted to help him know more.
And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue: whom when Aquila and Priscilla had heard, they took him unto them, and expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly.
They did it as a pair. Serving together can make a marriage stronger.

application.text: First, sit down with your spouse this week and talk about one goal you can paddle toward together. If you are not married, think of one goal you can share with a friend or family member.
Second, thank your spouse for one thing they do that you often overlook.
Third, if you feel the boat is drifting, speak with your bishop or branch president. They want to help.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that God designed marriage to bless His children. I know that He gives strength to couples who ask. I have felt the Holy Ghost guide a home. I know that Jesus Christ is the center of lasting love. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: When builders make a bridge over a wide river, they often start from both banks. Two crews work toward each other. They have to line up the pieces with great care. If they do, the two halves meet in the middle and the bridge holds.
Marriage is built the same way. Two people come from different places. Slowly, with care, they meet in the middle and build something strong.

mainMessage.text: A lasting marriage is built, piece by piece, by two people who love the Savior. It takes patience, the help of the Holy Ghost and hope. And it keeps being built for a lifetime.

blocks.text: **Two crews, one bridge.** Neither crew builds the bridge alone. Husband and wife each bring their part. They stand as equals, building toward the same goal.
And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.
Elder Ulisses Soares, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “In Partnership with the Lord” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
They walk side by side, as equals, the divine offspring of God.
Two halves make one bridge.
**A bridge needs upkeep.** Good bridges are checked and repaired for years. A marriage also needs steady care. It is never finished, and that is not bad news. It means there is always room to grow.
Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.
Elder Neil L. Andersen, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Eternal marriage is an eternal journey.
The care never stops.
**The strongest steel.** What holds a bridge together is the steel inside it. In marriage, that steel is the love of Christ. The more we love Him, the stronger our bond grows.
But charity is the pure love of Christ, and it endureth forever; and whoso is found possessed of it at the last day, it shall be well with him.
Elder Neil L. Andersen, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
As we increase our love for the Savior, our love for each other grows.
His love is the steel inside.
**Wait for the concrete.** Concrete takes time to set. Rushing it only weakens it. Marriage is like that. Some things need to cure slowly, and patience lets them.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,
Elder Neil L. Andersen, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
There are times in our marriage that require a stellar dose of patience.
Good things set slowly.
**The blueprint.** Builders follow a plan. We have one too. The Holy Ghost helps a husband and wife see what to do next. When we ask for His help, we are building by the plan.
For behold, again I say unto you that if ye will enter in by the way, and receive the Holy Ghost, it will show unto you all things what ye should do.
Elder Neil L. Andersen, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
We profoundly need the gift of the Holy Ghost in our personal lives and in our marriage.
He helps us follow the plan.
**The far bank.** Builders keep going because they can see the other side. Hope is how a couple sees it. It is hope in each other and in Jesus Christ.
Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.
Elder Neil L. Andersen, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Keep your hope in each other and in Jesus Christ.
Hope helps us see the far bank.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they and their spouse, or a couple they know, worked through a problem and grew closer. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Adam and Eve

blocks.text: Adam and Eve left Eden and faced a hard world. They did not face it apart. They worked and worshipped together.
And Adam and Eve blessed the name of God, and they made all things known unto their sons and their daughters.
They built a home as a pair, with God at the center.

application.text: First, think of one small thing you could “build” in your marriage this week, such as a weekly check-in or a shared prayer. If you are not married, think of one way to build a bond with someone close to you.
Second, begin it, and keep it up for seven days.
Third, if there are cracks that feel too big to fix alone, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that a marriage built on Jesus Christ can stand. I know that He mends what is broken. I have seen couples grow closer through hard times. I know God hears the prayers of husbands and wives. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

versions.analogy: A bridge built from both banks

opening.text: A good loaf of sourdough bread cannot be rushed. The starter needs days to grow. The dough needs hours to rise. If you hurry it, the bread comes out flat. But if you wait, and keep feeding it, it becomes something warm and good.
Marriage is a lot like that. The best parts often take time.

mainMessage.text: A marriage grows slowly, with daily care. Love for the Savior feeds it. Patience lets it rise. The Holy Ghost shows us what it needs. Hope keeps us going when the results are not yet visible.

blocks.text: **Two hands in the dough.** Good bread is shaped by hands that work together. Husband and wife shape their marriage side by side. No one stands above the other.
And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.
Elder Ulisses Soares, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “In Partnership with the Lord” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
They walk side by side, as equals, the divine offspring of God.
Two sets of hands, one loaf.
**A starter that keeps living.** A sourdough starter is fed again and again. It is never done. In the same way, marriage is something we keep feeding, not something we finish.
Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.
Elder Neil L. Andersen, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Eternal marriage is an eternal journey.
We keep feeding it.
**What we feed it.** A starter grows on flour and water. A marriage grows on love for the Savior. When that love rises, so does our love for each other.
But charity is the pure love of Christ, and it endureth forever; and whoso is found possessed of it at the last day, it shall be well with him.
Elder Neil L. Andersen, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
As we increase our love for the Savior, our love for each other grows.
Christ’s love is what we feed on.
**Let it rise.** Nobody can speed up the rising. The baker waits. So does a husband or wife during a slow season. Patience is a gift that lets the good things grow.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,
Elder Neil L. Andersen, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
There are times in our marriage that require a stellar dose of patience.
We wait, and it rises.
**Check the oven.** An experienced baker knows when the bread is ready. The Holy Ghost knows what our marriage needs. We can ask Him, and He will show us.
For behold, again I say unto you that if ye will enter in by the way, and receive the Holy Ghost, it will show unto you all things what ye should do.
Elder Neil L. Andersen, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
We profoundly need the gift of the Holy Ghost in our personal lives and in our marriage.
He knows what is needed.
**The smell of fresh bread.** Bakers smile when they think of the finished loaf. Hope is like that. It lets a couple look past a hard week and trust that good things are coming.
Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.
Elder Neil L. Andersen, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Keep your hope in each other and in Jesus Christ.
Hope lets us trust what is coming.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when patience in a marriage paid off. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Lehi and Sariah

blocks.text: Sariah worried deeply when her sons were gone on a dangerous errand. When they returned, she and Lehi were filled with joy.

And it came to pass that after we had come down into the wilderness unto our father, behold, he was filled with joy, and also my mother, Sariah, was exceedingly glad, for she truly had mourned because of us.
They faced fear and waiting together, and they shared the joy when it ended.

application.text: First, ask yourself where you have been rushing. Choose one thing in your marriage, or another close relationship, to be patient with this week.
Second, say a short prayer each day for your spouse or loved one.
Third, if a long wait feels too heavy, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that good marriages grow with time and with God’s help. I know that patience is a gift of the Spirit. I have felt hope return after a hard season. I know that Jesus Christ blesses those who trust Him. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: Two travelers share one map and one compass. They do not always agree on the route. But if they check the compass together, they find the way. The map does not lie, and the compass always points north.
A good marriage works this way. Two people, one direction, and a guide they both trust.

mainMessage.text: A marriage points in the right direction when both people follow the Savior. His love is the compass. Patience helps us wait out the wrong turns. The Holy Ghost shows the path. Hope keeps us moving.

blocks.text: **Two travelers, one road.** A husband and wife travel as equals. One does not lead while the other trails. They share the map and decide the road together.
And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.
Elder Ulisses Soares, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “In Partnership with the Lord” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
They walk side by side, as equals, the divine offspring of God.
We travel as equals.
**The road goes on.** A long road has many towns. Marriage has many seasons. Young love, busy years, quiet years. All of them are part of one journey.
Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.
Elder Neil L. Andersen, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Eternal marriage is an eternal journey.
Every season belongs to the journey.
**The compass.** A compass always points the same way. For a couple, love for the Savior is that fixed point. When we turn toward Him, our love for each other grows.
But charity is the pure love of Christ, and it endureth forever; and whoso is found possessed of it at the last day, it shall be well with him.
Elder Neil L. Andersen, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
As we increase our love for the Savior, our love for each other grows.
He is the fixed point.
**Wrong turns.** Every traveler takes a wrong turn now and then. Patience lets us go back and try again without blame. It is part of the journey, not the end of it.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,
Elder Neil L. Andersen, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
There are times in our marriage that require a stellar dose of patience.
Patience lets us turn around and try again.
**Ask for directions.** Wise travelers ask for help. A couple can ask the Holy Ghost. He gives guidance to husbands and wives who invite Him into their home.
For behold, again I say unto you that if ye will enter in by the way, and receive the Holy Ghost, it will show unto you all things what ye should do.
Elder Neil L. Andersen, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
We profoundly need the gift of the Holy Ghost in our personal lives and in our marriage.
We can ask, and He answers.
**The destination.** Travelers press on because the destination is worth it. For a couple, hope is the belief that they can be together and be happy. It is hope in each other and in the Savior.
Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.
Elder Neil L. Andersen, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey” from the April 2026 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Keep your hope in each other and in Jesus Christ.
Hope keeps us traveling.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they and their spouse found their way together after a hard choice. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Zacharias and Elisabeth

blocks.text: Zacharias and Elisabeth were an older couple. They stayed faithful to God for many years, even without the blessing they most wanted.

There was in the days of Herod, the king of Judaea, a certain priest named Zacharias, of the course of Abia: and his wife was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elisabeth. And they were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless.
They walked the same road for a lifetime, and God did not forget them.

application.text: First, ask your spouse, or a close friend or family member, “Where do you feel we are headed?” Listen well.
Second, name one way to turn toward the Savior together this week, such as scripture reading or a prayer.
Third, if you feel lost in your marriage, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that Jesus Christ is the way. I know that He can guide a husband and wife through any season. I have seen hope renewed in a home that turned to Him. I know that God loves every marriage that seeks Him. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.
